articles.title: The best places to celebrate Halloween in Norway this year
articles.content:
Add a comment
                                                                                            
                                        
                                                                        
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                
                            
                        
                    
                    
                    
                            
                            We've compiled a list of must-visit Halloween events in Norway that will satisfy your Halloween itch. Photo by Sergio Zhukov on Unsplash
                    
                                            
                            
        
            
            
            
            
        
        Add The Local as a preferred source
    
                        
                                        
                        As the leaves turn and the crisp autumn air settles in, Norway's cities come alive with bustling Halloween festivities. We've put together a selection of the spookiest and most entertaining events across the country.

As the air chills and leaves turn, the entire country gears up to celebrate All Saints' Eve, better known as Halloween, on the evening of October 31st (preceding the Christian holiday of All Hallows' Day on November 1st).

In Norway, children celebrate by donning costumes and embarking on a "trick or treat" adventure, knocking on neighbourhood doors with the light on to collect candies, while adults usually opt for Halloween parties and activities.

Whether you're searching for a spine-tingling scare or simply want to embrace the festive autumn spirit, we've compiled a list of must-visit Halloween events in Norway's big cities that will satisfy your Halloween itch.

READ MORE: How Norway adopted the American tradition of Halloween

In Oslo, the celebration begins at the Norwegian Folk Museum, where the Halloween weekend is filled with events that combine spine-chilling themes with rich cultural traditions. Families can choose between Day of the Dead, The Haunted City and The Dark Valley this year.

Deichman libraries are also organising free Halloween activities for children and families across several locations in Oslo. The programme features workshops and drawing challenges, alongside events for adults, including an autumn walk featuring spooky stories.

As Halloween night itself approaches, the Technical Museum transforms into a venue for adult festivities on October 31st. The evening features a Halloween quiz, screenings of classic horror films, VR horror experiences, and an eerie mix of music by DJ Pavlo, ranging from satanic boogie to horror disco.

Until November 1st , Frøya Park at Skarpsno is hosting a Halloween park with decorated tunnels, live horrific characters, circus performers, and light installations.

Oslo's festivities continue with two concerts by the Oslo Symphony Orchestra, with both film and classical music that will put you in the Halloween mood. Organisers encourage attendes to come in their best costume.

TusenFryd, located just 20 kilometres south of Oslo in Vinterbro, is Norway's largest amusement park and has become a beloved Halloween destination over the past few years, though visitors should check availability, as tickets for several time slots are already sold out.

For those seeking adult-themed entertainment, a wide variety of costume and themed parties will be hosted in bars and venues across the city. Just search on Facebook, or their websites.

Bergen's festivities begin with two nights of activities at Mount Fløyen on October 30th and 31st, including a walk through a haunted path, where witches and other spooky creatures can appear when you least expect it.

On October 30th, visitors can enjoy Halloween-themed decor and surprises at the Bergen Aquarium, perfect for a family day out.

The University Museum of Bergen will explore the darker side of nature with family activities, including live blood-sucking insects under microscopes, taxidermy demonstrations, and a hen-mummification workshop.

Additionally, VilVite, Bergen's science centre, caters to families with a special Halloween show and immersive evening experiences.

For party fans aged 20 and over, Social House is hosting the "Garden of Evil" at Teknostallen, featuring guest DJs, visual shows, and a mandatory costume policy.

For those looking for an adrenaline-packed Halloween, a paddle trip along the Nidelva , organised by Tronheimkajakk, invites participants to kayak through a ghostly scene adorned with lights and shadows, offering discounts to those in costume.

Stavanger gears up for what is billed as one of Norway's biggest Halloween parties on October 31st at Fiskepiren.

Fiskepiren, a concert stage and social hub in the heart of Stavanger, will transform into the ultimate Halloween venue. Expect a night of shows and surprises featuring performances by artists like Tom Boye and Doc Lello.

The Stavanger Symphony Orchestra is also bringing some of the most eerie scores in cinema history to life at Stavanger Konserthus on Friday 30th and Saturday 31st .

On Halloween itself, Bjergstedparken will be transformed into a "witch's forest", open to families brave enough to explore - all as part of the Grøss Festival, which runs until November 1st.

Discover the spooky side of the Arctic capital with the 'Mystical Halloween Tromsø' guided walk. Organised by the Troll Museum, the tour explores local myths and legends about ghosts, trolls, huldras and other supernatural creatures from Northern Norway.

Do you know about another Halloween-themed event in Norway which we haven't mentioned? Let us know.

articles.title: The reasons Norway might reject your Norwegian citizenship application
articles.content:
1 comment
                                                                                            
                                        
                                                                        
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                
                            
                        
                    
                    
                    
                            
                            There are a number of reasons why the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) will reject a citizenship application. Photo by Mark König on Unsplash
                    
                                            
                            
        
            
            
            
            
        
        Add The Local as a preferred source
    
                        
                                        
                        Norwegian citizenship comes with a hefty application fee and plenty of requirements. There are several reasons why the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration might reject an application.

Lifetime enrollment in the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme, the ability to live in Norway for as long as you wish, and returning to Norway after a few years away without going through the immigration process are some of the many benefits of Norwegian citizenship.

Norwegian citizenship doesn’t come easy, though. In addition to waiting years to become eligible, you will have to pass language and citizenship tests, provide a criminal record certificate, verify your identity and meet the requirements for permanent residence if you don’t hold it already.

This is all before you pay 6,500 kroner to apply for Norwegian citizenship.

So, what are the reasons why the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) turns down applications?

This applies not just to your citizenship application but also to your entire stay. If you bend the rules when it comes to the residence requirements, you could find your citizenship application rejected.

Even if your application is successful, you will find your citizenship revoked later if the UDI finds out. The UDI will still revoke your citizenship, even if you are the one who decides to come clean to them.

Should the authorities have reason to believe that you have provided incorrect information on any residence or citizenship applications, they will typically invite you for an interview with the police or notify you of your revocation in advance.

READ MORE: How Norway can revoke residency and citizenship over wrong details

This one might seem obvious, but it can happen relatively easily. One of the most common reasons for a foreign national having their citizenship rejected is not passing the citizenship or social studies test (in Norwegian).

For the citizenship test, you must answer 24 out of 36 multiple-choice questions correctly.

The social studies test is taken by those who typically have been through the social studies course for immigrants.

Language-wise, you will generally have to have passed an oral test in Norwegian at  B1 level.

Another common pitfall is the criminal record certificate. Criminal record certificates are only valid for three months. The certification proves that you haven’t been convicted of any crimes and are not disqualified from applying for citizenship.

As the certificate can only be valid for three months, the UDI advises that you shouldn’t order the certificate until you have an appointment to hand in your documents to the police. This reduces the likelihood of the certificate expiring before your documents are handed in.

Failure to meet any of the citizenship requirements will result in your application being turned down. You must also hold a valid residence permit whilst applying for citizenship.

Remember that under standard rules, you must have stayed in Norway for a total of eight of the past eleven years and held residence permits that were each valid for at least one year.

On the UDI website, you can learn how to calculate residence periods in exception cases. However, as there is currently a proposal to amend the Citizenship Act, which could alter how qualifying residence time is measured, these requirements may change in the future.

READ MORE: What will Norway's plan to toughen citizenship rules mean for you?

Being convicted of a criminal offence that results in a fine or prison sentence will bar you from being eligible for citizenship for a set period of time.

The disqualification period can range from 2.5 years up to 39 years, depending on the severity of your punishment. You can see an overview of the disqualification rules on the UDI website.

Those who have received fixed penalty notices rather than criminal fines will not be disqualified. Those who have had charges or cases dropped are also not disqualified.

An example of a fixed penalty notice would be a fine for minor or moderate speeding.

To be eligible for citizenship, you also need to be eligible for permanent residence at the same time, which can make matters confusing.

For many, the easiest way around this is to just hold permanent residence as proof of eligibility while applying for citizenship.

The key thing to look out for when it comes to citizenship is the minimum income requirements for non-EEA permanent residence applicants.

One of the requirements for permanent residence applications for non-EEA nationals is that you will need to have fulfilled the income requirements for the previous 12 months and that you cannot have received financial assistance (økonomisk sosialhjelp) during the prior 12 months.

Skarstein satt i Oslo bystyre for Ap i perioden 2015–2019.

articles.title: Norway's sovereign wealth fund loses over $30 billion in 3rd quarter
articles.content:
Add a comment
                                                                                            
                                        
                                                                        
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                
                            
                        
                    
                    
                    
                            
                            Stacks of Norwegian 500-kroner banknotes. Photo: Norges Bank norges-bank.no
                    
                                            
                            
        
            
            
            
            
        
        Add The Local as a preferred source
    
                        
                                        
                        Norway's sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest with assets of more than $2 trillion, on Thursday reported a negative return of 278 billion kroner ($31 billion) in the third quarter as it was weighed down by higher interest rates.

It posted a negative return of 0.5 percent in the quarter, dragged down by a negative return of 3.5 percent in its fixed-income investments, while its equity and property portfolios increased by 0.5 percent and 0.4 percent respectively.

"The fund's return was close to flat, ending slightly negative as rising interest rates led to weaker results on our fixed-income investments," the fund's deputy CEO Trond Grande said in a statement.

Invested primarily in equities, bonds and real estate across the globe, the fund reported a value of 22,014 billion kroner at the end of September.

Inflation around the world, fuelled in particular by soaring energy prices linked to the conflict in the Middle East, has led several central banks, including the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, to raise interest rates in the third quarter.

"Equity returns were also close to zero, but there were large differences between sectors. Energy companies rose the most, while interest-rate-sensitive sectors such as utilities and real estate fell," Grande said.

Fuelled by the Nordic country's oil revenues, the fund is invested in more than 7,100 companies spanning the globe, and holds around 1.5 percent of all listed companies worldwide, making it the world's largest single investor.

articles.title: IN DATA: Who were the 5,000 foreigners deported from Norway last year?
articles.content:
Add a comment
                                                                                            
                                        
                                                                        
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                
                            
                        
                    
                    
                    
                            
                            In 2025, Norwegian authorities issued formal deportation orders (utvisningsvedtak) to 5,002 foreign nationals. Photo by Blake Guidry on Unsplash
                    
                                            
                            
        
            
            
            
            
        
        Add The Local as a preferred source
    
                        
                                        
                        As well as tracking how many people move to Norway, the Directorate of Immigration (UDI) also monitors foreign nationals ordered to leave the country (with British citizens throwing up a surprise).

In 2025, Norwegian authorities issued formal deportation orders (utvisningsvedtak) to 5,002 foreign nationals, according to statistics from UDI.

A deportation order in Norway carries a formal entry ban, which prevents the person from returning to Norway for a certain period, or permanently in serious cases. It can even include a ban from entering the Schengen Area.

One of the main reasons a foreign resident can be deported from Norway is breaking the Immigration Act. This includes administrative violations like overstaying a visa, working without a valid permit, giving false information on residency applications, or not leaving the country after an asylum or visa refusal.

In 2025, 4,125 orders (which represents 82.5 percent of the total deportation orders) were issued on these grounds.

Foreign nationals can also be expelled from Norway after a criminal conviction, but this is much less common. Last year there were 368 such cases (7.4 percent of all deportation orders).

Contrary to popular belief, EU citizens are not exempt from being expelled from Norway, even though they have freedom of movement under the EEA Agreement.

In 2025, 500 orders (10 percent of all cases) were issued to European nationals. This can happen on grounds such as public order, public security, or abuse of rights.

In 2025, most deportation orders were given to nationals from South Asia and West Africa.

India had the highest number of cases with 949 in total. Of these, 941 were for immigration breaches and eight for criminal convictions. Pakistan was next with 918 orders, 917 for immigration breaches and one for a criminal conviction.

There was then a sharp drop. Bangladesh came third with 331 orders (329 for immigration breaches and two for criminal offences), and Nigeria in fourth place with 227 orders (218 for immigration breaches and nine for criminal convictions).

Combined, nationals from these four countries made up nearly 49 percent of all deportation orders in Norway in 2025.

Further down the overall list among non-EEA states were countries like Kenya with 112, Nepal (139), Ghana (111), China (78), the UK (62), Ukraine (59), and the United States with 42.

Australia and Canada recorded just 8 and 10 orders, respectively.

Among the European nationals, the highest number of expulsion orders was issued to citizens from Romania (160), Lithuania (89), Poland (75), and neighbouring Sweden (64), followed by the Netherlands (20), Latvia (13), and Spain (12).

UK nationals top list of convicted criminals deported

The figures show an unexpected trend in criminal deportations. Of the 62 British citizens ordered to leave in 2025, 35 were deported after criminal convictions. This made the UK the country with the most convicted criminals deported from Norway last year, ahead of Ukraine (33), China (31), and the United States (19).

A further 25 Britons were expelled for immigration status violations after losing EU freedom of movement post-Brexit.

READ ALSO: Indians, Brits and Syrians top Norway's permanent residency list

UDI statistics show a steady increase in expulsions in recent years.

Norwegian authorities recorded 1,210 deportation orders in 2021, 1,894 in 2022, 2,893 in 2023, and 3,302 in 2024. With the total passing the 5,000 mark in 2025, expulsion orders were more than four times higher than four years prior.

articles.title: Direktør trekker seg fra Holocaustsenteret
articles.content:
Direktør Jan Heiret ved Holocaustsenteret går av med umiddelbar virkning.

Grunnen er et vanskelig forhold mellom Heiret og jødiske trossamfunn, heter det i en pressemelding fra HL-senteret, som er det formelle navnet på Holocaustsenteret.

Det var Vårt Land og Khrono som omtalte saken først.

– Det har over tid utviklet seg et vanskelig forhold mellom direktøren og jødiske trossamfunn i Norge. HL-senteret er avhengig av tillit i disse institusjonene, som var med å opprette senteret som et forsknings- og formidlingssenter med et bredt mandat, heter det i pressemeldingen.

Heiret sier han opplever at styret ikke lenger støtter ham i den situasjonen som har oppstått.

– Uten en slik støtte er det umulig å gjøre en god jobb som leder av senteret. Derfor har jeg kommet til at jeg må tre til side, sier han.

Heiret tiltrådte som direktør for HL-senteret 1. januar 2024.

Skoler og barnehager holdes stengt, og kokevarselet opprettholdes. Finnmarkssykehuset har satt rød beredskap, og om lag 150 pasientavtaler blir berørt.

articles.content:
Venezuelas opposisjonsleder og fredsprisvinner María Corina Machado er tilbake i landet, melder nyhetsbyrået Reuters.

– Venezuela! Jeg er så glad for å kunne kunngjøre at vår leder, min kjære Maria Corina, er tilbake på venezuelansk jord, skriver en av hennes allierte Edmundo González på X.

Han republiserer en X-melding fra Machado hvor hun skriver «Jeg er her. Med dere.»

Machado har i en periode levd i eksil i Panama. Hun har vært borte fra Venezuela i rundt ett år.

Venezuela

Natt til 25. juni ble Venezuela rammet av to store jordskjelv. Over 6100 mennesker er bekreftet omkommet. Naturkatastrofen har forverret situasjonen i det allerede kriserammede landet.

articles.title: Netanyahu advarer mot nytt holocaust om han ikke blir valgt
articles.content:
To dager før valget i Israel skjerper statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu retorikken ytterligere.

I et innlegg på X advarer Netanyahu om et nytt holocaust dersom han ikke blir gjenvalgt.

– Alle som bryr seg om sin egen, sin families og sine kjæres fysiske eksistens, bør få skjelve på hendene før de stemmer på noen som ikke vil være i stand til å fullføre oppgaven – og dermed dømme seg selv og familien til faren for et nytt holocaust, skriver han.

Netanyahu har lagt ved et KI-generert bilde av en atomeksplosjon i det sentrale Israel.

Iran

Iran er en islamsk republikk i Midtøsten. Siden 28. februar har landet vært i krig med USA og Israel. Samtidig har det siden slutten av 2025 vært store demonstrasjoner mot det ultrakonservative, undertrykkende regimet i landet.

articles.title: Bolsonaro har avgitt stemme
articles.content:
Flávio Bolsonaro har avgitt stemme i Brasil, og sier «tiden er inne for reell endring», melder AFP.

Velgerne skal velge mellom den sittende venstreorienterte presidenten Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva og hans høyreorienterte utfordrer Flávio Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro, sønn av den ytre høyre-orienterte tidligere presidenten Jair Bolsonaro, er en knapp favoritt til å vinne presidentvalgets andre runde mot Lula, som forsøker å sikre seg en fjerde, ikke-sammenhengende presidentperiode.

Brasil

President Lula da Silva vant presidentvalget i Brasil i oktober og ble innsatt 1. januar 2023. 8. januar gikk støttespillere av tidligere president Jair Bolsonaro til angrep på Kongressen, presidentpalasset og høyesterett i hoevdstaden Brasília.

articles.title: Sterk vind fører til innstilte avganger ved Schiphol
articles.content:
Amsterdam lufthavn Schiphol, en av Europas travleste knutepunkter, innstilte titalls flyvninger søndag som følge av kraftig vind forårsaket av stormen Boelo.

AFP talte rundt 90 kansellerte avganger på flyplassens nettsider søndag, hovedsakelig til europeiske byer som Paris, Roma og Dublin. Titalls ankomster til flyplassen ble også innstilt eller forsinket.

«På grunn av sterk vind forventes færre flyvninger å ta av og lande søndag 25. oktober,» opplyste flyplassen.

Det ble ikke oppgitt nøyaktig hvor mange flyvninger som var berørt.

articles.title: Boelo førte til omfattende strømbrudd i Storbritannia
articles.content:
Titusenvis av briter var uten strøm søndag mens stormen Boelo rammet de nordlige delene av Storbritannia med kraftig vind og styrtregn, melder AFP.

Stormen førte også til store forstyrrelser i reiseliv og samferdsel.

Boelo er sesongens andre navngitte storm i Storbritannia og følger tett etter den første – stormen Austen, som brakte med seg kraftige vindkast til de sørlige delene av landet fredag.

Mer enn 82 000 eiendommer sto uten strøm klokken 08.00 (08.00 GMT), opplyste bransjeorganisasjonen Energy Networks Association i en oppdatering.

articles.title: Stormen «Boelo» har truffet: Bølgeblikk og stålplater på avveie
articles.content:
På Karmøy har politiet fått melding om bølgeblikkplater som har flydd av et tak.

– Platene kommer fra et industribygg tilhørende kommunen. Kommunen reiser ut til stedet, skriver operasjonsleder Rune Tallaksen i loggen like før klokken 3.

I Bergen har vinden revet løs stålplater fra et mindre næringsbygg.

– Brannvesenet er på vei til stedet for å prøve å sikre disse. Blåser kraftig på stedet, skriver operasjonsleder Tore Fanebust like etter klokken 3.

På forhånd er det meldt om mye vind og regn, og det er sendt ut oransje farevarsel for jord- og flomskred på store deler av Østlandet.

Stormen traff Norge natt til søndag. NVE har sendt ut oransje farevarsel om flom- og jordskredfare for deler av Østlandet.

articles.title: Eksplosjoner hørt i Riyadh – houtiene advarer mot å bruke flyplassen
articles.content:
Houthi-opprørerne i Jemen advarte natt til søndag flyselskaper, ansatte og passasjerer mot å bruke flyplassen i Saudi-Arabias hovedstad Riyadh.

Advarselen kom samme kveld som flyplassen kunngjorde at to terminaler tas i bruk for både innenriks- og utenlandsflyvninger fra søndag.

Dette er ikke første gang den iranstøttede bevegelsen kommer med slike trusler. Tidligere i oktober ble 12 drept og over 300 såret i et angrep.

Noen timer etter advarslen meldte den saudiledede koalisjonen at de hadde skutt ned et ballistisk missil på vei mot Riyadh. Tre eksplosjoner kunne høres over byen, melder nyhetsbyrået AFP.

Saudi-Arabia

Saudi-Arabia er et dypt religiøst monarki i Midtøsten. Det islamske landet er ofte kritisert for at kvinner har svært innskrenkede rettigheter. Landet har enorme oljeforekomster.

articles.title: Kraftig turbulens hindrer redningshelikopter – ni personer værfast på fjellet
articles.content:
Et turfølge på ni personer har søndag morgen bedt om hjelp i fjellet over Kinsarvik og Lofthus på Vestlandet.

Kraftig turbulens gjør at redningshelikopteret ikke klarer å ta seg frem til stedet.

– Skal være ni personer i følget. Nokså sikker posisjon på dem. Opplyst at telt er ødelagt, og at de er våte og kalde, skriver politiet i loggen.

– HRS har sendt melding til turfølget og bedt de gå i retning Kinsarvik og går Røde Kors mannskap i møte.

Også en hundepatrulje fra politiet er på vei til Kinsarvik. Disse vil gå turfølget i møte sammen med frivillige mannskaper fra Røde Kors og Norsk Folkehjelp.

articles.title: Milliardforlik i overgrepssak mot den katolske kirken i New York
articles.content:
Det katolske erkebispedømmet i New York har godkjent et forlik verdt rundt 8 milliarder kroner til ofre for seksuelle overgrep begått av geistlige.

Ifølge New York Times får hvert av de rundt 1300 ofrene minst 250.000 dollar – drøyt 2,3 millioner kroner – men basert på hvor alvorlige overgrep det er snakk om, kan noen også få mer. Til sammen er forliket på drøyt 800 millioner dollar.

Etter at gravejournalister avdekket overgrep mot tusenvis av barn i den katolske kirken, har flere bispedømmer i USA måttet betale millionbeløp i erstatninger.

Overgrep i den katolske kirke

Den katolske kirke har de siste årene fått mange anklager om seksuelt misbruk av barn rettet mot seg. Pave Frans har fordømt enhver form for overgrep, og sier kirken har et ansvar for å beskytte barn og sårbare voksne.

articles.title: Obama langer ut mot Trump: – Kaos, grusomhet og korrupsjon
articles.content:
USAs tidligere president Barack Obama gikk lørdag hardt ut mot etterfølgeren Donald Trump.

– Etter to år med kaos, grusomhet, korrupsjon og inkompetanse, har vi nå sjansen til å si at nok er nok, sa Obama i sin tale.

Uttalelsen kom under et valgmøte i Ohio til støtte for demokratiske kandidater før mellomvalget 3. november.

Ekspresidenten ga Trump-administrasjonen skylden for økt prisvekst, som er en av de viktigste sakene for velgerne før de stemmer om halvannen uke.

– Den nåværende presidenten velger å ta en rekke dårlige beslutninger. Viktigst av alt er at han har valgt å starte en unødvendig krig som ingen har bedt om.

Mellomvalg i USA

Det er mellomvalg tirsdag 3. november. 435 plasser i Representanthuset og 35 av 100 plasser i Senatet står på valg.

articles.title: Minst tre drept av russisk drone i Dnipropetrovsk
articles.content:
Tre personer ble drept da en russisk drone rammet Dnipropetrovsk sørøst i Ukraina lørdag, opplyser guvernøren i fylket.

Minst åtte andre ble såret, deriblant ei elleve år gammel jente, ifølge meldingen.

Krigen i Ukraina

Russland invaderte Krim og deler av fylkene Luhansk og Donetsk i Øst-Ukraina i 2014. 24. februar 2022 gikk Russland til fullskala invasjon. Krigen medfører store militære tap og rammer sivile hardt.
